title: Vulcan VC6L Amazon Leo LV-01 (SLC-41)
t0_note: ULA Vulcan Leo 1 page: Friday, Nov. 13 at 12:54 p.m. EST (1754 UTC). FAA operations advisory ULA KV-01 primary 11/13/26 1754Z-1900Z, backup 11/14/26 1732Z-1838Z. LL2 id ef9850ad-1096-425b-9d27-f7bbd186e61a, status Go, window 17:54–18:24Z (checked 2026-11-11).

azimuth_deg.derived: great-circle bearing from the LL2 pad (28.58341025N, 80.58303644W) to the far-edge midpoint (36.3583N, 70.9750W) of NAVAREA IV 1078/26 Area A, the launch corridor (times 131754Z-131932Z Nov and daily backups matching the FAA KV-01 window). Area A far-edge mid gives a non-rotating inclination of ~52.66 deg vs the 51.9 deg Amazon Leo / Kuiper shell (and KA-01 insertion). Area B (near-shore drop) 44.09 deg / i~52.34; Area C (south of Newfoundland, same notice, matches CZQM H7357/26) 44.32 deg / i~52.16. Geometric azimuth for i=51.9 deg from this pad is 44.64 deg. Hazard-area azimuth kept (NOTAM-first). Source: https://space-notices.com/notice/nav-warning-NAVAREA%20IV%201078%2F26 UPDATE 2026-11-12: ULA published the target inclination 51.9 deg (https://x.com/ulalaunch/status/2120895023067639859); azimuth intentionally kept NOTAM-first, so the sim inclination residual vs 51.9 deg is reported in the notes.

payload_kg.note: FITTED within 10.0–27.2 t so the ASSUMED MES1 duration delivers the ASSUMED 180 × 460 km transfer. 40-satellite stack mass unpublished; result is NOT an estimate of the real payload.

insertion_alt_km.assumption: LV-01 parking/transfer perigee unpublished. 180 km is a labelled stand-in for a two-burn ascent to the published ~460 km near-circular insertion (apogee set to the published 460 km).

apoapsis_alt_km.note: ULA (2026-11-12): LV-01 targets a 'near-circular low Earth orbit of approximately 285 miles (460km) inclined at 51.9 degrees'. Replaces the earlier 450 km ASSUMPTION from Amazon KA-01. 460 km treated as circular (near-circular, eccentricity unpublished). Inclination is steered by the NAVAREA IV 1078/26 azimuth, not retuned to the published 51.9 deg; residual is reported.

target.altitude_reference: equatorial-radius (r - 6378.137 km) for SMA; insertion altitude residual uses geodetic altitude

header_notes: PRE-FLIGHT ILLUSTRATIVE. ULA Vulcan VC6L, first 6-SRB / first LEO-optimized Centaur V flight, 40 Amazon Leo satellites from SLC-41, T0 2026-11-13T17:54:00Z (Fri Nov 13 9:54 a.m. PST).

Booster/Centaur event times are ULA UG Fig. 2.1.1-2 TYPICAL CCSFS values (Approximate Times), not this flight. MES1 cutoff is an ASSUMED 600 s burn (T+908 s), tuned toward a 180 × 460 km transfer. MES2 (circularize to 460 km) is modelled at first apoapsis in post_cutoff. Deploy time for LV-01 is not in a first-hand source retrieved this turn, so after MES2 the stage is propagated +2 revs on the inferred insertion orbit.

TARGET UPDATED 2026-11-12: ULA published 'near-circular low Earth orbit of approximately 285 miles (460km) inclined at 51.9 degrees' (https://x.com/ulalaunch/status/2120895023067639859); replaces the ASSUMED 450 km KA-01 analog.

final_cutoff_s.assumption: MES1 cutoff = typical MES1 ignition 308 s + ASSUMED 600 s first burn; see vehicle Centaur cutoff_s. Tuned if needed so the transfer apogee is near 460 km.

fairing_jettison_s.src: https://www.ulalaunch.com/docs/default-source/rockets/2023_vulcan_user_guide.pdf Fig. 2.1.1-2 PLF jettison T+00:05:16 (typical CCSFS example)

burns.name: MES2 (Centaur V circularization)

isp_s.assumption: same RL10C 453.8 s as the vehicle file (Wikipedia / L3Harris, secondary)

target_perigee_km.derived: ULA-published ~460 km near-circular insertion (replaces 450 km KA-01 analog); duration of MES2 is solved so perigee reaches 460 km

burns.basis: LV-01 burn 2 time unpublished. ULA UG: one or two Centaur burns are typical for LEO. MES2 is flown at first apoapsis after the ASSUMED 180 × 460 km MES1 transfer, open thrust, duration solved to 460 km perigee (circularize).

deploy.note: LV-01 payload-separation time is not in a first-hand ULA/Amazon/FCC document retrieved this turn (a NSF-forum quotation of a ULA STA giving first sep at ~1 h 17 min was not independently verified). After MES2 the stage is propagated 2 revs on the inferred 460 km insertion orbit.

notes: ULA (2026-11-12): 'near-circular low Earth orbit of approximately 285 miles (460km) inclined at 51.9 degrees' (https://x.com/ulalaunch/status/2120895023067639859). This LV-01 sim uses 460 km circular as the insertion target (replacing the earlier 450 km KA-01 analog) and the NAVAREA IV 1078/26 corridor azimuth (i~52.7 deg non-rotating) without retuning to 51.9 deg.
Centaur disposal (HYDROPAC 3246/26 Eastern Indian Ocean, ~T+2.5 h, matching the FAA-window backups) is not modelled; the file ends 2 revs after MES2.

fitted.method: scipy least_squares (TRF, bounded) vs published knots + target orbit

payload_kg.basis: 40 Amazon Leo satellites, mass unpublished (Amazon says production sats weigh more than 1,000 lb / 450 kg → 18 t floor before dispenser). Upper bound = UG/fact-sheet VC6 LEO PSW 27,200 kg (200 km / 28.7°). Fitted payload is NOT an estimate of the real stack.
